metadata.common_names: English oak, pedunculate oak, common oak

data.habitat_ai: High-canopy woodlands, coppice, wood pasture, deciduous and mixed forests, hedges, margins of swamps, rivers, and ponds in temperate regions
data.ecological_function_ai: Keystone species supporting over 2300 associated species including insects (400+ herbivores), birds, mammals, lichens, bryophytes; acorns feed jays, squirrels, deer; leaf litter enriches soil; provides nesting/roosting sites for birds and bats
data.native_adapted_habitats_ai: Most of Europe (British Isles to Caucasus), western Asia; temperate deciduous forests, woodlands on clay and loamy soils
data.agroforestry_use_cases_ai: Timber production, coppicing/pollarding for fuel/fencing/baskets, wood pasture/silvopasture, fodder (acorns/leaves), hedges, compost activator from bark/leaves
data.general_description_ai: Large deciduous tree up to 40m tall with stout trunk up to 11m girth, broad spreading unevenly domed crown, greyish-brown fissured bark, alternate lobed leaves, wind-pollinated catkins, pedunculate acorns; long-lived hardwood species
data.compatible_soil_types_ai: Moist well-drained loams, clay, heavy soils; pH 5.0-8.0 (acid to alkaline tolerant); prefers deep fertile neutral loams, avoids prolonged waterlogging, acid peat, shallow limestone; drought tolerant once established
data.growth_form_ai: Large tree with short stout trunk, massive lower branches, broad spreading rounded to unevenly domed crown
data.leaf_type_ai: Alternate, oblong-ovate 10-12cm long x 7-8cm wide, short 2-3mm petiole, cordate base, 3-6 rounded lobes to midrib, dark green above paler below, glabrous or few hairs
data.flower_color_ai: Yellowish male catkins, inconspicuous brownish female flowers
data.fruit_type_ai: Ovoid acorns 1.5-4cm long maturing brown-black, in shallow warty cups, clusters of 2-3 on 4-8cm peduncles
data.bark_characteristics_ai: Greyish-brown, closely grooved with vertical plates, deeply furrowed on mature trees; thick corky bark on older trees
data.lifespan_ai: Long-lived; typically 400-500 years, up to 1000+ years
data.stewardship_best_practices_ai: Full sun, well-drained soil; slow-growing; transplant young; avoid root disturbance; maintain health to resist pests; coppice/pollard every 50 years if needed
data.planting_recipes_ai: Sow fresh acorns autumn in outdoor beds or deep pots (protect from rodents); plant permanently young due to taproot; full sun, moist well-drained soil; forestry density e.g., thin to 2000/ha by age 20
data.pruning_maintenance_ai: Prune dormant season (late winter/early spring) to avoid oak wilt/beetles; structural pruning young for strong form; remove dead/diseased/crossing branches; no more than 30% canopy/year
data.disease_pest_management_ai: Diseases: acute/chronic oak decline, powdery mildew, oak wilt, anthracnose; Pests: oak processionary moth, galls (wasps), caterpillars (winter moth etc.), borers on stressed trees; promote health, prune dormant, monitor, fungicides if needed
data.fire_management_ai: Mature trees fire-tolerant due to thick corky bark; young regenerate from base; low-severity fires historically maintained oak forests; suitable for post-fire reforestation
data.cultural_significance_ai: National emblem of England; sacred to Druids (oak groves, mistletoe), Thor/Zeus/Jupiter (thunder god tree); symbol of strength/royalty (crowns); used in myths (world tree), Bach remedies, historical timber for ships/buildings
